neighbours.label: the abstract noun before a 'that' clause stating a claim (the idea that, the fact that)
fire: Recent findings also support the idea that memory fades slowly.
Her accent betrays the fact that she grew up abroad.
New data challenge the notion that bees need flowers.
The report ignores the fact that wages have fallen.
Critics reject the idea that art must be useful.
His silence reveals the fact that he knew all along.
Tests confirm the theory that the river moved west.
This supports the view that exercise helps the brain.
quiet: Recent visitors also liked the museum that opened last year.
Her accent is the one that I heard abroad.
New farmers plant the flowers that bees visit.
The report describes the factory that closed in May.
Critics praised the painting that hung in the hall.
His silence ended the meeting that began at noon.
Tests confirm the bridge that crosses the river is safe.
This is the gym that helps the team.

notes: Card: ' implies' x2, ' idea', ' spirit', 'ism', ' why', ' fact'. Probes: ' fact' 0.495, ' idea' 0.322, ' spirit' 0.091, ' why' under 0.06; 'the team that we hired' 0.025. Near misses keep 'that' after concrete nouns.
